news.title: NIH NCATS publishes Nature Medicine: deep-learning screen of 12,456 compounds surfaces 3 Alzheimer’s/Parkinson’s repurposing candidates at 98% accuracy
news.summary: The NIH National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS) announced May 22, 2026 — and published in Nature Medicine — that an AI-driven drug-repurposing initiative launched in 2024 identified three experimental compounds that show promise in early-stage neurodegenerative disease models. The model is a deep-learning architecture trained on 20 years of failed clinical trials, animal studies, and molecular interaction data; it screened 12,456 compounds and reported 98% preclinical-screening accuracy — the first time AI has hit that threshold on this task. Headline result: finerenone, originally approved for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, reduced amyloid plaque buildup by 42% in a 12-week mouse Alzheimer’s model. Two other candidates were originally developed for cardiovascular and metabolic disorders.
news.why_it_matters: AI-doing-science as a curve dimension finally moves on a primary scientific result, not corporate framing. The corpus shape is the trick: training on failure surfaced what twenty years of human trial-and-error iteration missed. The 12,456-compound search space is small by industrial-screening standards, but the recovery of a repurposing candidate at the molecular-target level — finerenone hitting amyloid in a mouse model at 42% — is the kind of result that justifies the AlphaEvolve-style framing of AI as a novel-discovery instrument. The repurposing path also compresses the FDA timeline: finerenone already has safety data. If candidates clear Phase I/II in neurodegenerative indications, AI-doing-science has shipped its first commercially-actionable medicine.
news.verdict: First clean AI-doing-science primary result of the month. SP-Index +1.
news.evidence: Time News primary writeup + NIH NCATS announcement + Nature Medicine publication.
news.tap_next: Watch for: (a) the Nature Medicine paper DOI surfacing; (b) NCATS Phase I/II timeline for finerenone; (c) whether the model architecture or weights get published; (d) other labs replicating the train-on-failure corpus design.

news.title: SpaceX publicly files S-1 under ticker SPCX — $1.75T valuation, $75B raise, June 12 Nasdaq target — AI exposure direct via xAI absorption + $40B Anthropic compute
news.summary: SpaceX formally filed its S-1 with the SEC on May 20, 2026 and confirmed plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX. The Nasdaq debut is targeted for June 12 at a $1.75 trillion valuation and a $75 billion raise — which would more than double Saudi Aramco’s 2020 record as the largest IPO in history. Lead underwriters: Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, BofA, Citi, JPMorgan. The S-1’s AI-infrastructure exposure is direct: xAI was absorbed in February 2026, the four-year $40B+ Anthropic compute commitment ($1.25B/month through May 2029) shows up as a related-party contract, and Starlink runs at roughly a $20B revenue annualized rate. The filing closes the third leg of the week’s capital-substrate triple-wave alongside OpenAI’s Friday confidential filing and Anthropic’s October window.
news.why_it_matters: Three of the largest AI-infrastructure names — measured by either model capability or supply-side compute — walked toward the public markets in eight days. SpaceX is the supply-side bet (compute substrate at hyperscale), OpenAI is the frontier-capability bet, Anthropic is the enterprise-adoption bet. The buy-side investor base on listing day will set the public valuation floor for all three trades and, by extension, for every adjacent AI-infrastructure name. The Anthropic related-party contract surfacing in the SpaceX S-1 also means Anthropic’s October window now has cross-disclosure obligations that did not exist a week ago.
news.verdict: Capital substrate triple-wave complete. Largest week of AI-infrastructure capital formation on record.
news.evidence: Bloomberg primary + TechCrunch S-1 teardown + The VC Corner full breakdown + multiple secondary.
news.tap_next: Watch for: (a) SPCX pricing day June 11-12; (b) updated SEC S-1 amendments with revised Anthropic compute disclosures; (c) Anthropic response to the related-party language; (d) OpenAI public S-1 surfacing late July or August.

news.title: Ramp May 2026 AI Index confirms enterprise flip: Anthropic 34.4% vs OpenAI 32.3% — first crossover, Claude Code is the engine, OpenAI peaked mid-2025
news.summary: The Ramp May 2026 AI Index — Ramp processes corporate-card spend across more than 50,000 U.S. businesses — reports Anthropic enterprise adoption rose 3.8% in April to 34.4% of businesses while OpenAI fell 2.9% to 32.3%. First crossover since the index began. Anthropic has quadrupled business adoption over the past year; OpenAI added 0.3 percentage points. The growth engine is Claude Code — Ramp commentary pegs it at approximately 4% of all public GitHub commits worldwide. OpenAI enterprise adoption peaked near 36.5% in mid-2025 and has been declining since. The same Ramp report warns Anthropic’s lead may be fragile (escalating costs, compute constraints, token-pricing model fragility).
news.why_it_matters: Capital substrate now has a buy-side proof point that did not exist for any previous frontier-AI funding round. Anthropic’s October IPO window pitches into a market where the enterprise daily-driver share is already structurally with them — and where Claude Code is the canonical proof of agentic-coding economic value (Spotify 4,500 deploys/day; engineers have not coded since December). The Ramp curve is also the visible context for the WSJ-surfaced Q2 $10.9B revenue projection: the financial statement is the trailing indicator of the adoption flip. For OpenAI’s confidential S-1 process, the Ramp data is the most likely first risk-factor line item from underwriters: we are no longer the enterprise daily-driver.
news.verdict: Buy-side structural anchor for the triple-wave IPO trajectory. Enterprise-adoption dimension added to the SP-Index.
news.evidence: Ramp AI Index primary data + VentureBeat + TechCrunch + Axios + multiple secondary.
news.tap_next: Watch: (a) the June Ramp AI Index for whether the crossover holds or reverts; (b) OpenAI counter-positioning press on enterprise customer wins; (c) any S-1 risk-factor language on token-based pricing model durability.

news.title: Figure F.03 livestream past 48 hours of continuous operation — endurance proof holds, rate-per-package disclosure remains the open question
news.summary: Figure AI continuous-operation livestream of F.03 humanoids sorting packages has now run past 48 hours with no logged failure since the May 13 start. After the May 17-18 Man vs. Machine 10-hour contest where intern Aimé Gérard edged the robots 12,924 to 12,732 (2.79s/package vs 2.83s/package) and CEO Brett Adcock posted “last human victory,” the demonstration shifted to demonstrating sustained autonomous endurance without disclosed throughput-rate or interventions-per-hour numbers. Viewers have continued to name the visible units (Bob, Frank, Gary nameplates added). Adcock posting cadence on day-by-day endurance milestones (day 6, 8, 9, now 10+) has been the public proxy for the run health.
news.why_it_matters: Embodied deployment as a curve dimension keeps moving on endurance, not yet on rate. Endurance answers can the humanoid stay up 48 hours? Rate answers is the humanoid economically competitive with $15/hour human labor? The former is necessary, the latter is sufficient. As long as Figure publishes only the endurance milestone and not the per-package-cost numbers, the curve nudge is bounded.
news.verdict: Endurance proof holds. Rate verdict still open.
news.evidence: Interesting Engineering coverage + PANews + Technology.org + TechRadar critical read + Glitchwire community thread.
news.tap_next: Watch: (a) any disclosed rate-per-package or interventions-per-hour metric; (b) the run-length termination event; (c) Helix-02 neural network architecture details; (d) Polymarket Figure-related markets.
